steps.title: This is Elastic
steps.say: Elastic is a **driver dashboard**: the screen drivers look at during a match. You build it from the values your robot publishes.

steps.title: Robot code first
steps.say: Elastic shows live values, so your robot code needs to be running. If it isn't yet, press **Start** here and wait for it to say Running.

steps.title: Connection
steps.say: Down here it says **Network Tables: Connected** once Elastic can see your robot. Red means it can't, so check that your code is running.

steps.title: Dashboard tabs
steps.say: Each tab is one page of the dashboard. Teams usually keep one for **Autonomous** and one for **Teleoperated**.

steps.title: Add or switch tabs
steps.say: The **+** adds a tab, and the arrows move between them.

steps.title: Add Widget
steps.say: **Add Widget** lists everything your robot publishes. Drag a value onto the grid to show it. Elastic picks a widget to match, like a number, a toggle, or a graph.

steps.title: The grid
steps.say: Widgets snap to this grid. Drag one to move it, drag its corner to resize it, and right-click it to change what kind of widget it is.

steps.title: Settings
steps.say: **Settings** changes the grid size, colors, and how often values update.

steps.title: Saving
steps.say: Use **File → Save Layout** to keep your dashboard. Then it's still there the next time you open Elastic.
